reasons: No tests or checks for the addresses or the lists are visible.
Addresses are not verified by the code, and at least one (the China regulator entry) looks mismatched to its name.
Unknown industries get an empty result rather than wrong content, which is the intended behavior.

terms.meaning: A named bundle of organizations or feeds the app offers as a starting point for one industry.
A number from 1 to 4 that rates how official or reliable a source is. The code does not say which end is best, but the data suggests 1 is highest.
A machine-readable feed of news items that other programs can read automatically.
Engineering, procurement and construction: the firms that design and build a plant.
Liquefied natural gas: natural gas cooled to liquid form so it can be shipped.
A lookup table that connects each industry name to the packs that belong to it.
The main home address of an organization, rather than a deep link to one page.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Importing the wind source pack
sections.what: Brings in the wind industry's source pack from its own file so it can be listed alongside the others.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps wind sources in their own file.
sections.watch_out: If that file moves or renames its export, this file will stop working.

sections.name: PackSource
sections.title: Shape of one source
sections.what: Describes one organization or feed the app can read: its name, address, type (feed, web page or API), trust tier, category and region.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code, but the fields suggest a ranked list of reference and news sites.
sections.watch_out: The code does not say which direction the trust numbers run, so the meaning must be checked against the data.

sections.name: SourcePack
sections.title: Shape of a named source pack
sections.what: A named bundle with a title, a description, a count and the list of sources. This is what appears as one pack on the screen.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: regulators
sections.title: Nuclear regulators list
sections.what: The nuclear regulators and safety authorities, such as the IAEA, the US NRC and many national bodies, each with its address, type, trust tier and region.
sections.why: Likely reason: regulators are kept as their own group, separate from companies and news.
sections.watch_out: Some addresses may not match their agency names, such as the China entry, so check them before relying on them.

sections.name: operators
sections.title: Nuclear operators list
sections.what: Nuclear plant owners and utilities, such as EDF, Constellation, KEPCO and CNNC, each with its address and region.
sections.why: Likely reason: plant owners are grouped apart from regulators and suppliers.
sections.watch_out: The addresses are typed in by hand and nothing checks them, so a company that moves its website will break its link without warning.

sections.name: vendors
sections.title: Nuclear vendors list
sections.what: Reactor designers, fuel makers and technology suppliers, such as Westinghouse, Framatome, Rosatom, NuScale and Cameco.
sections.why: Likely reason: technology and fuel makers form their own group.
sections.watch_out: Trust tiers here are hand-set opinions, and nothing in the code checks or updates them.

sections.name: epc
sections.title: Nuclear builders list
sections.what: Engineering and construction firms that build nuclear plants, such as Bechtel, Jacobs, AtkinsRéalis and Hyundai E&C.
sections.why: Likely reason: builders are listed separately from owners and suppliers.
sections.watch_out: Bechtel and Saipem also appear in the LNG builder list, so one company can show up in two industries.

sections.name: news
sections.title: Nuclear news and associations list
sections.what: Industry news sites, trade groups and government energy pages, such as World Nuclear News, the Nuclear Energy Institute and the US DOE pages.
sections.why: Likely reason: news and member groups are kept separate from companies and regulators.
sections.watch_out: Several sites appear twice, once as a web page and once as a feed, so the same source can be counted twice.

sections.name: NUCLEAR_SOURCE_PACKS
sections.title: The five nuclear packs
sections.what: Defines the five nuclear packs shown on screen (regulators, operators, vendors, builders, news), each with a plain description and a count.
sections.why: Likely reason: groups the separate lists into named packs for the screen.
sections.watch_out: The descriptions are typed by hand and name only some companies, so they can drift from the real lists.

sections.name: lngRegulators
sections.title: LNG regulators list
sections.what: Gas and LNG regulators and agencies, such as FERC, the US DOE fossil energy office, PHMSA, the IEA and ACER.
sections.why: Likely reason: the same grouping idea as nuclear, applied to LNG.
sections.watch_out: The file comment asks that only real organizations with top-level addresses be added, but the code does not enforce this.

sections.name: lngOperators
sections.title: LNG operators list
sections.what: LNG plant owners and developers, such as QatarEnergy, Cheniere, Shell, ExxonMobil and Woodside, each with its address and region.
sections.why: Likely reason: owners are grouped apart from builders and suppliers.

sections.name: lngEpcTechnology
sections.title: LNG builders and technology list
sections.what: Builders and technology suppliers for LNG plants, such as Bechtel Energy, Technip Energies, Air Products, Linde and GTT.
sections.why: Likely reason: construction firms and technology licensors are combined into one group.
sections.watch_out: Bechtel and Saipem appear here and also in the nuclear builder list, so their counts are kept separately for each industry.

sections.name: lngNews
sections.title: LNG news and associations list
sections.what: LNG industry groups and news sources, such as the International Gas Union, GIIGNL, LNG Prime, Argus and Reuters Energy.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps LNG news separate from nuclear news.

sections.name: LNG_SOURCE_PACKS
sections.title: The four LNG packs
sections.what: Defines the four LNG packs shown on screen (regulators, operators, builders and technology, news), each with a description and a count.
sections.why: Likely reason: mirrors the nuclear layout so the screen handles both industries the same way.

sections.name: SOURCE_PACKS_BY_INDUSTRY
sections.title: Industry registry
sections.what: Maps each industry name to its packs: nuclear, LNG and renewables (wind only). Any industry not listed gets no packs.
sections.why: The file comment says industries without entries should show an honest empty state, never nuclear content.
sections.watch_out: A new industry shows nothing until it is added to this map.

sections.name: getSourcePacksForIndustry
sections.title: Looking up packs for an industry
sections.what: Returns the packs for one industry name, or an empty list when that industry has none.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps unknown industries from failing, so the page can show an empty state as the registry comment requests.
sections.watch_out: The name is not checked, so a misspelled industry name returns an empty result without any error.

summary: Holds the built-in lists of nuclear and LNG organizations (regulators, companies, news sites) that the app offers as starting source packs, plus a registry that maps each industry to its packs.
purpose: Gives the owner ready-made lists of trusted sources to research from, so they do not have to type each one in.
why: Likely reason: the app needs curated starting sources for each industry. The comments say the lists contain only real organizations with stable top-level web addresses, but the reason for the trust tiers is not stated.
how: First brings in the wind source pack from its own file. Then defines a list of sources for each nuclear group, followed by the LNG groups. Each pack bundles its list with a title, a description and a count. A registry maps industry names to their packs. A small lookup function returns the packs for one industry, or an empty list if there are none.
inputs: An industry name (slug) such as nuclear, lng or renewables, passed to the lookup function. The source lists themselves are typed directly into this file.
outputs: A list of source packs. Each pack has an id, name, description, count and its sources. Each source has an id, name, feed or web type, address, trust tier, category and region.
risks: Addresses are typed by hand and never checked, so some may be wrong or out of date, and a broken link fails without any message. The trust tiers are hand-set opinions. Some organizations appear in two industries, so their counts overlap. Some addresses look mismatched to their names, for example the China nuclear regulator entry points to a government environment ministry page.
debug: If a pack list is empty, check that the industry name matches a key in the registry in this file. If a source link fails, open its address in a browser and then edit its entry here. If the wind pack is missing, check the import at the top of the file and the file it points to. If a count looks wrong, count the entries in that list, because the count is calculated from the list.
